journal_name: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications

abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel paradigm shift in wireless communications by establishing a unified mathematical framework for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in 6G networks. Unlike conventional approaches that treat sensing and communication as separate subsystems, we propose a bidirectional information theory that jointly characterizes the fundamental trade-offs between estimation accuracy and data rate. By introducing the concept of mutual information coupling coefficient, we derive closed-form expressions for the capacity-accuracy frontier under various channel conditions. Our theoretical analysis reveals that joint optimization can achieve up to 40% spectrum efficiency improvement compared to traditional separated architectures. Furthermore, we introduce a probabilistic beamforming design that adapts to dynamic environment characteristics. The proposed framework provides rigorous mathematical foundations for future mobile networks to implement native sensing capabilities. Simulation results validate our theoretical derivations and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed paradigm in urban vehicular networks scenarios. This work fundamentally advances communication theory by redefining the information-theoretic limits for future wireless systems with integrated functionalities.

This paper presents an enhanced optimization framework for network slicing resource allocation in 5G mobile networks, addressing the critical challenge of dynamic resource partitioning across heterogeneous services. We develop a Lyapunov-based stochastic optimization model that jointly considers latency requirements, energy efficiency, and resource utilization fairness. The proposed algorithm employs a novel drift-plus-penalty technique with adaptive weight tuning to balance conflicting objectives in real-time network slicing scenarios. Our theoretical analysis proves the algorithm achieves O(1/V) time-average optimality gap with O(V) convergence speed, significantly outperforming existing methods that typically exhibit O(ε^(-2)) complexity. We further derive closed-form expressions for the optimal slicing ratios under Poisson traffic arrivals. Numerical results demonstrate that our approach reduces average latency by 35% while improving energy efficiency by 28% compared to state-of-the-art baselines in edge computing scenarios. The mathematical framework provides rigorous performance guarantees suitable for practical implementation in software-defined networking environments.

We present MetaNet, a revolutionary network architecture design that transcends the limitations of conventional software-defined networking through native intelligence integration. MetaNet introduces a hierarchical control plane that embeds machine learning capabilities directly into network function virtualization infrastructure, enabling self-organizing network behavior at unprecedented scales. The proposed architecture implements a three-tier intelligence hierarchy: edge agents perform real-time traffic classification, regional controllers execute medium-term resource optimization, and a global orchestrator handles long-term topology management. We design novel northbound and southbound interfaces that support both traditional OpenFlow protocols and emerging intent-based networking paradigms. A full prototype implementation demonstrates that MetaNet achieves sub-millisecond control loop closure while maintaining 99.999% network availability. Performance evaluation across diverse scenarios including vehicular networks and industrial IoT deployments validates the system's adaptability and robustness. The architecture fundamentally transforms network management by shifting from reactive configuration to proactive optimization, establishing a new design paradigm for future mobile network infrastructure.

This paper proposes an enhanced protocol stack design for reliable V2X communications in autonomous vehicular networks, significantly advancing existing Dedicated Short-Range Communications (DSRC) and Cellular-V2X (C-V2X) standards. Our proposed Adaptive Multi-Mode V2X (AMV2X) system introduces a novel dual-mode transceiver architecture that seamlessly switches between distributed contention-based and centralized scheduling-based access mechanisms based on real-time channel conditions and application requirements. We implement an advanced channel congestion control algorithm that dynamically adjusts transmission parameters using reinforcement learning, achieving substantial improvements in safety-critical message delivery reliability. The complete protocol stack design includes an optimized medium access control layer, an enhanced physical layer abstraction, and a cross-layer security mechanism leveraging physical layer characteristics. Comprehensive performance evaluation through both ns-3 simulation and field trials demonstrates that AMV2X reduces end-to-end latency by 45% and improves packet delivery ratio by 30% in dense urban scenarios compared to current 5G-based V2X implementations. The proposed system maintains backward compatibility with existing C-V2X standards.
